tests.title: --effort is registered as a string flag with DeclareEnum listing the seven accepted values
given: a fresh flag.FlagSet with Common.Register called
tests.when: the flag set is inspected
then: a flag named effort exists with type string and empty default
the enum metadata for effort lists off, minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max
tests.pseudocode:
fs := flag.NewFlagSet("t", flag.ContinueOnError)
c := &Common{}
c.Register(fs)
f := fs.Lookup("effort")
assert f != nil
assert f.DefValue == ""
assert enumValues(fs, "effort") == ["off","minimal","low","medium","high","xhigh","max"]

no field named Variant exists

c := Common{}

tests.title: Effort precedence: flag > env > tier > unset, as a table test
given: a stubbed catalog that resolves tier names and model ids
a stubbed ClampThinkingLevel that returns the input level unchanged
tests.when: ResolveModelNamed is called with combinations: (1) --effort=low with tier STANDARD, (2) no flag but AF_MODEL_EFFORT=low with tier STANDARD, (3) no flag, no env, tier STANDARD (tier's own high), (4) no flag, no env, model id (ThinkingUnset)
then: case 1: effective effort is low (flag wins over tier's high)
case 2: effective effort is low (env wins over tier's high)
case 3: effective effort is high (tier's own)
case 4: effective effort is ThinkingUnset

tests.title: An invalid --effort value exits 2 and lists the accepted values

fs := flag.NewFlagSet("t", flag.ContinueOnError)

c.Register(fs)

assert strings.Contains(err.Error(), "max")

tests.title: When clamping changes the level, an effort_clamped warning is recorded naming both levels and the model
given: a model that supports only medium and high

then: a warning with code effort_clamped is recorded
the warning message names the requested level (xhigh)
the warning message names the clamped level (high)
the warning message names the model
tests.pseudocode:
c := &Common{Effort: "xhigh", Model: "test/limited-model"}
choice, err := c.ResolveModelNamed("test/limited-model")
assert err == nil
assert choice.Thinking == ThinkingHigh
w := run.Warnings()
assert any(w, func(w Warning) bool { return w.Code == WarnEffortClamped })
assert strings.Contains(w[0].Message, "xhigh")
assert strings.Contains(w[0].Message, "high")
assert strings.Contains(w[0].Message, "test/limited-model")

tests.title: Repair effort precedence: --repair-model-effort > repair model's tier effort > run's effort
